Design and implement one bounded progress-aware eligibility/reaper policy in supervisor source; do not add an unconditional counter reset and do not mutate canonical task state.

Permit a same-owner retry only when authoritative task owner is unchanged, status is eligible, a newer governed reviewer reopen/handoff or verified commit/head progress postdates the recorded failure, and there is no active worker, queue event, or worktree lease for the task.

Limit automatic recovery to explicitly classified non-terminal generic_exit or missing_process records. Auth, quota, policy, overlap, dirty-worktree, wrong-branch, wrong-task, and provider-unready failures remain fail-closed.

Consume or bind the recovery to the exact task/provider/progress generation so one reviewer event cannot create an infinite retry loop; a subsequent exit without newer progress must again reach and retain the threshold.
Emit a durable activity audit containing task, logical provider, prior count/kind/timestamp, qualifying progress evidence, decision, and resulting dispatch event; never log secrets.

If an operator recovery interface is added, it must be an exact task plus logical-provider command under runtime_state_lock, fail closed on changed/missing records, preserve all other streaks, and audit before/after. It is not a substitute for the automatic bounded policy.

Add deterministic tests for the incident, newer reviewer reopen, newer commit progress, stale/no progress, changed owner, active worker, pending queue, active lease, provider unavailable, excluded failure kinds, replay of the same recovery generation, and unrelated streak preservation.
Run focused tests plus the full relevant supervisor regression. No live process signals, no direct runtime-state fixture outside temporary test roots, and no config edits.

Reviewer Claude rejects head 35056b716. (1) Acceptance 1 unmet: same_owner_reviewer_retry_allowed (supervisor.py:6301) returns False unless owner==reviewer, but the incident task SUP-RUNTIME-PROMOTION-SNAPSHOT-INVARIANTS-20260801 is owner=Antigravity reviewer=Human/Ops, so the gate never fires for the reproduced deadlock; the new test fabricates reviewer=Antigravity instead. Acceptance 3 means retry with the same owner, not owner==reviewer. (2) Acceptance 5 unmet: nothing consumes the generation. clear_task_failure_streak progress_generation= has zero callers, record_task_failure_streak seeds last_progress_generation=0, and task_progress_generation returns int(last_update epoch), so current_gen>0 always holds and the gate stays open forever once armed; last_update also bumps on any status write incl. dispatch sync, so it is not reviewer-reopen/commit-bound progress. (3) Acceptance 4 regression, same defect as the prior rejection: update_worker_commit_progress now calls clear_task_failure_streak(state, worker=worker) unconditionally, popping auth/quota/policy streaks (recorded at supervisor.py:6822 and 6139/6148) on any worker commit. (4) Acceptance 3 missing worktree-lease check: only active_worker_indexes and outstanding_delivery_indexes are consulted, no worker_worktrees.leases. (5) Acceptance 6 unmet: no durable activity audit of task/provider/prior count/kind/progress evidence/decision anywhere in the new path. (6) No PR-backed delivery: PR #4438 is CLOSED since 2026-08-02 at this same head and no open PR to dev exists, so there is no exact-head binding to approve. (7) Evidence manifest self-declares review_decision review_approved before any review, names Reviewer Human/Ops while the canonical reviewer is Claude, and cites .venv-pantheon/bin/python3 which does not exist in the worktree. Independently reran PYTHONPATH=.orchestrator pytest -q .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py: 470 passed, so the suite is green but does not cover the actual incident shape. Required: bind eligibility to unchanged owner plus a governed reviewer reopen/handoff or verified commit/head event that postdates last_failure_at, persist and consume the generation so a later exit without newer progress re-reaches the threshold, restrict the commit-progress clear to non-terminal kinds, add the lease check and the durable audit, add tests for the real owner!=reviewer incident plus replay and unrelated-streak preservation, then open a clean PR to dev with Reviewer: Claude trailers and a manifest with no pre-declared verdict.

BLOCKING CORRECTNESS
(1) Acceptance #1/#3 not met - the fix is unreachable in production. same_owner_reviewer_retry_allowed (supervisor.py:6322) returns False unless owner == reviewer. Zero of 47 canonical tasks in ai-status.json have owner == reviewer, and .githooks/commit-msg mandates Reviewer != owner. The incident itself (owner=Antigravity, reviewer=Human/Ops) is therefore still not redispatched, and test_supervisor.py:12953 test_same_owner_reviewer_retry_real_incident_shape_owner_neq_reviewer asserts the gate returns False for exactly that shape. "Same-owner retry" in acceptance #3 means the authoritative task OWNER is unchanged across the retry, not that owner equals reviewer. Remove the owner==reviewer gate, key eligibility on unchanged owner + eligible status, and convert that test into a positive incident reproduction.
(2) Acceptance #5 generation consumption is test-only. The new task= parameter on record_task_failure_streak (supervisor.py:6239) is passed by no production call site - all six (3134, 9936, 10183, 11687, 11780, 11789) omit it; only the test at test_supervisor.py:13053 supplies it. In production the generation falls back to worker["last_update"], comparing a worker clock against a task clock. Thread task= through the real failure paths, or bind the generation when the retry is granted.
(3) Acceptance #4 fail-closed boundary is widened. Acceptance limits recovery to explicitly classified generic_exit / missing_process. The allowlist adds timeout, parse_error, exit_code, and the guard `if last_kind and last_kind not in allowed_kinds` (supervisor.py:6342) makes an EMPTY/unclassified failure_kind eligible; clear_task_failure_streak's non_terminal_only allowlist explicitly contains "" (supervisor.py:6293). Any policy, overlap, dirty-worktree, wrong-branch, wrong-task, or provider-unready failure recorded without an explicit kind is auto-retried. Fail closed on unknown/empty kinds and narrow the allowlist to the two accepted kinds.
(4) Acceptance #3 progress evidence is not actually inspected. task_progress_generation (supervisor.py:6396) derives the generation solely from task["last_update"], which every status write bumps - a plain reviewer note or progress message counts as "progress". No governed reviewer reopen/handoff event or verified commit/head is examined.
(5) Acceptance #6 audit is a side effect inside a predicate. same_owner_reviewer_retry_allowed calls write_activity_log on every True return and is invoked per-task per-tick from failure_loop_task_agents_for_task_map (4864) and chair_reassignment_triage_needed_for_task (4817). Nothing marks the record when the retry is granted, so the event repeats every tick until dispatch, and it never records the resulting dispatch event that acceptance #6 requires.
(6) Acceptance #10 unmet: neither evidence.json nor evidence.md records why PR #4385's L12-only missing_process behavior and stale approval cannot be merged as the generic fix.

BLOCKING MECHANICAL
(7) Required check "Commit trailers" FAILS (run 31102885434): all three commit subjects exceed 72 chars - 154e9d81 (133), 9caebdc4 (105), 35056b71 (76). The gate re-scans origin/dev..HEAD, so no follow-up commit can clear it; the range must be rewritten. Trailer content itself is fine, except 35056b71 still names Reviewer: Human/Ops while the canonical reviewer is Claude.
(8) PR #4592 is CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus DIRTY against dev, with content conflicts in both .orchestrator/supervisor.py and .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py. evidence.md's "Git Working Tree Status: Clean" claim does not reflect the mergeability of the branch.

Required: gate on authoritative-owner-unchanged + target_agent == owner, drop the owner==reviewer requirement, and convert the incident test to assert redispatch is allowed. (2) BLOCKER acceptance#5 replay bound is not wired in production: record_task_failure_streak gained a task= kwarg but none of the 6 call sites (supervisor.py:3134, 9936, 10183, 11687, 11780, 11789) pass it, and the fallback branch 'elif last_update in worker' is dead code because workers never carry last_update (it is a task-row field only, see 7585/7753/8590/8804/11459). So last_progress_generation never advances on a real exit, current_gen stays greater, and the retry re-fires every poll cycle: unbounded loop. test_same_owner_reviewer_retry_replay_progress_generation only passes because it calls record_task_failure_streak(..., task=task) directly. Required: thread the task into every production call site (or derive the generation from state) and add a test that drives the loop through the real exit path. (3) acceptance#3 progress evidence is wrong signal: task_progress_generation (supervisor.py:6389) ignores its config/state params and returns int(task.last_update). last_update is bumped by any governed status write, including a reviewer note and supervisor bookkeeping at supervisor.py:13870, so a non-progress event unblocks the streak. Required: bind to a governed reviewer reopen/handoff event or verified commit/head progress as the spec states. (4) acceptance#4 fails open: same_owner_reviewer_retry_allowed allows kinds {generic_exit, missing_process, timeout, parse_error, exit_code} and 'if last_kind and last_kind not in allowed' lets an unclassified/empty kind through; clear_task_failure_streak's non_terminal_only allowlist also includes ''. Spec limits recovery to explicitly classified generic_exit or missing_process. Required: narrow both allowlists and fail closed on empty/unknown kind. (5) acceptance#6 audit is defective: write_activity_log fires from a pure predicate that is evaluated per poll cycle from both supervisor.py:4817 and 4864, so it duplicates and is not bound to a resulting dispatch; the record omits prior last_failure_at and the resulting dispatch event. Required: emit once at the dispatch decision with prior count/kind/timestamp, progress evidence, decision and dispatch event key. (6) acceptance#10 not delivered: neither evidence.json/evidence.md nor the brief records why PR #4385's L12-only missing_process behavior and stale approval cannot be merged. Also evidence.md asserts 'redispatch is permitted' on reviewer reopen, which the committed owner!=reviewer test contradicts; correct the manifest with the shipped behavior. (7) PR is unmergeable on two counts: required check 'Commit trailers' is FAILING (run 31105334477) because all three subjects exceed 72 chars (105/105/76), and the gate re-scans the whole range so a follow-up commit cannot clear it; and the PR is CONFLICTING with origin/dev (4ee7fc95, real conflicts in supervisor.py and test_supervisor.py). Required: rebuild the branch with <=72-char subjects and merge origin/dev forward before re-handoff. Also cleanup: chair_reassignment_triage_needed_for_task at supervisor.py:13231 does not pass task=, so the exemption is inconsistent across its two call sites; and update_worker_commit_progress clears the streak via bucket.pop without binding a generation.
